A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same M4-RAG study. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and supplementary Sections 7–11 are readable and support reliable comparison after matching reordered material.

before.justification: v1 reports original VQA experiments across 11 models on CVQA and WORLDCUISINES, retrieval-quality analyses, and human validation of model judging.

after.justification: v2 retains the original benchmark results and additionally reports human verification of 200 generated CVQA oracle captions in Section 8.1.

M1.justification: The retrieval-generation pipeline and its four configurations remain unchanged. Naming the E5 text retriever and specifying that oracle captions use ground-truth answers clarify previously underspecified components; the PDFs do not establish a procedural replacement.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate CVQA and WORLDCUISINES with the same language inventory, source datasets, and retrieval-corpus counts. The new 189-country description and caption-validation study do not establish expanded benchmark coverage.

E2.justification: v2 adds Qwen3-VL 4B, 8B, and 30B-A3B to the CVQA retention/correction comparisons in Figures 4–5. Its Figure 6 also adds Pangea and the previously absent WORLDCUISINES Qwen3-VL 8B column. The primary accuracy tables retain the same comparators.

E3.justification: The new caption-validation protocol uses 200 randomly sampled pairs, four annotators, and a 1–5 relevance scale. Section 9.1 also changes its small/large model categories from below 7B/above 30B to below/above 14B. Existing VQA metrics and inference settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Section 8.1 adds a focused human check of whether generated oracle captions support answering CVQA questions. The retrieval-quality analysis extends to Qwen3-VL on CVQA, and the resource-group analysis fills model gaps. Existing oracle-gap and language-wise analyses remain.

E5.justification: Table 2 retains the same five agreement metrics, coefficients, and validation design of 100 samples per retriever with five raters. No new repeated-run, seed, or uncertainty-estimation procedure is documented. The caption audit's unanimous ratings are additional results.

E6.justification: All 176 accuracy entries in the matched Tables 3–4 are unchanged. v2 adds CVQA Qwen3-VL curves, missing heatmap entries, and the finding that all 200 audited captions received 5 with full agreement. Its new Section 4.4 attribution of a −32.4% drop to Qwen2.5-VL 32B conflicts with Figure 6, which assigns it to Gemma3 27B.

T1.justification: Equations 1–2 retain the same retrieval and conditional-generation definitions. Neither version contains additional theoretical propositions or proofs; notation edits and metric explanations do not change the mathematics.

C1.justification: The central benchmark, model-scaling, and multilingual-degradation claims remain. v2 adds an explicit 189-country coverage claim in the abstract and extends the conclusion to emphasize degradation even in models explicitly trained on multilingual data.

C2.justification: v2 adds interpretations concerning weaker retrievers amplifying model differences and Pangea's multilingual training failing to ensure context robustness. The conclusion develops specific recommendations for model-aware retrieval, joint retriever–VLM post-training, and test-time adaptation while retaining the original parametric-knowledge explanation.

D1.justification: Sections 2.3 and 3.1 newly specify Wikipedia section-based passage construction, content cleaning, deduplication across queries and languages, E5 text retrieval, and the inputs used to generate oracle captions. These are documentation additions; hardware, generation hyperparameters, prompt templates, and access links are retained.

R1.justification: The descriptive comparison in Table 1 substantially expands to include benchmarks such as TyDiQA, XOR QA, AfriQA, ViQuAE, Encyclopedic VQA, and MRAG-Bench. Section 5 adds extensive positioning against retrieval-augmented multimodal benchmarks and multilingual VLM families, substantially broadening the earlier discussion.

P1.justification: The introduction is extensively rewritten, explicit RQ1–RQ3 and Section 2.1 objective bullets are removed, and contributions, results discussion, and conclusion are substantially reorganized. Human evaluation gains separate subsections, and oracle/caption-query terminology is standardized throughout.

P2.justification: Figure 1 is redesigned around retrieval accuracy deltas and a revised explanatory diagram. The resource heatmap gains clearer grouping, colors, hatching, and model columns. Other plots receive revised legends, ordering, and styling; Table 1 expands, and the detailed results tables and language figures are reordered.

improvement.justification: v2 improves reproducibility through clearer corpus and retrieval details, adds targeted validation of oracle captions, and makes the analyses and research positioning more complete. The primary performance evidence remains unchanged. A new model-attribution error in Section 4.4 and retained overgeneralizations in Figure 3's caption limit the gains, but the added documentation and validation support a modest overall improvement.
